discord.slashCommand.description: Runs when someone uses one of your bot's slash commands in your Discord server, like /socials. Answer with the "Reply to slash command" step.

fields.command: The command name without the slash, like "socials". Several names separated by commas work too. Leave it empty to run for every command.

variables.command: The command that was used, without the slash, like socials
variables.option: What the person typed in the command's text box (empty when there is none)
variables.optionName: The name of that text box
variables.user: The person's name as the server shows it (their nickname if they have one)
variables.userId: Their Discord user ID. Handy for the "Give a role" step
variables.channelId: The ID of the channel where they used it
variables.channelName: The name of that channel, without the #
variables.discordInteractionId: Tells the "Reply to slash command" step which command use to answer. Leave it alone

discord.messagePosted.description: Runs when someone posts a message in a channel your bot can see. To read the text, tick "Message Content Intent" on the Discord bot page and in the Developer Portal.

fields.channel: Only messages in this channel. Pick it from the list or type its name, like #suggestions. Leave it empty for every channel.
fields.contains: Only messages with these words in them, like "!clip". Capital letters do not matter. Leave it empty for every message.

variables.message: What they wrote (empty unless Message Content Intent is switched on)
variables.user: The person's name as the server shows it

discord.memberJoined.description: Runs when someone joins your Discord server. Good for a welcome message or a starter role. Needs "Server Members Intent" switched on, on the Discord bot page and in the Developer Portal.

variables.mention: Pings them when put in a message, like "Welcome %mention%!"
variables.serverName: The name of the server they joined
variables.isBot: True when the new member is a bot

discord.connected.description: Runs when your Discord bot comes online in Cuebot.

discord.disconnected.description: Runs when your Discord bot goes offline, for example when the internet drops. Cuebot tries to bring it back by itself.

variables.reason: Why it went offline, in plain words

discord.sendMessage.description: Posts a message with your own Discord bot, like your "I'm live!" post. It can have an embed (a coloured box with a title, text and picture).

fields.channel: The channel to post in. Pick it from the list (it shows your bot's servers), or type its name like #announcements.
fields.text: The message, up to 2000 characters. %variables% work, like "I'm live! Come say hi, %user%". To ping a role, use <@&ROLE_ID>.
fields.embedTitle: The embed's title, like "I'm live!". Leave every embed box empty for a plain message.
fields.embedDescription: The text inside the embed. Can be long (up to 4096 characters).
fields.embedUrl: A web link: clicking the title opens it. Your stream link is a good choice.
fields.embedColor: The colour of the embed's edge, like #9146FF. Words work too: twitch, youtube, kick, red, green, blue, purple.
fields.embedImage: A web link to a picture shown big in the embed, like your stream thumbnail.
fields.rememberAs: A name like "live post". Cuebot saves where the message is under this name, so the edit or delete step can find it later, even after a restart.

variables.discordMessageLink: A link to the message that was posted
variables.discordChannelId: The ID of the channel it was posted in

discord.editMessage.description: Changes a message your bot posted earlier. Handy to turn your "I'm live!" post into "Stream ended, thanks for watching".

fields.message: Which message: the name you typed in "Remember it as" when posting it, like "live post". A message link works too.
fields.text: The new text. Leave it empty to keep the old text and change only the embed.
fields.embedTitle: The new embed title. Fill in any embed box to replace the whole embed.
fields.embedDescription: The new text inside the embed.
fields.embedUrl: The new link for the embed's title.
fields.embedColor: The new colour, like #808080 for grey.
fields.embedImage: A web link to a new picture.
fields.removeEmbed: Tick to take the embed off the message (when you leave the embed boxes empty).

discord.deleteMessage.description: Deletes a message your bot posted earlier.

fields.message: Which message: the name you typed in "Remember it as" when posting it, like "live post". A message link works too.

discord.addRole.description: Gives someone a role in your Discord server, like "Live notifications". The bot's own role must be above that role in Server Settings, Roles.

fields.member: Who gets the role: %userId% from a Discord trigger, a user ID, or their name in the server.
fields.role: The role to give. Pick it from the list or type its name exactly.
fields.reason: A note shown in your server's audit log, like "Asked with /notify". You can leave it empty.

discord.removeRole.description: Takes a role away from someone in your Discord server. The bot's own role must be above that role in Server Settings, Roles.

fields.member: Who loses the role: %userId% from a Discord trigger, a user ID, or their name in the server.
fields.role: The role to take away. Pick it from the list or type its name exactly.
fields.reason: A note shown in your server's audit log. You can leave it empty.

discord.replyToSlashCommand.description: Answers the slash command that started this action. Using it twice sends a second message. Without it the bot answers with the default reply.

fields.text: The answer, up to 2000 characters, like "Find me on twitch.tv/yourname".
fields.embedTitle: An embed title for the answer. Leave every embed box empty for plain text.
fields.embedUrl: A web link: clicking the title opens it.
fields.embedColor: The colour of the embed's edge, like #9146FF.
fields.embedImage: A web link to a picture shown in the embed.
fields.interaction: Which command use to answer. Leave it as %discordInteractionId%.

discord.sendDirectMessage.description: Sends a private message from your bot to one person in your server. Some people block messages from servers, so it may not arrive.

fields.member: Who gets it: %userId% from a Discord trigger, a user ID, or their name in your server.
fields.text: The message, up to 2000 characters. %variables% work here.

discord.setStatus.description: Changes what people see under your bot's name, like "Watching my stream". Needs the bot to be connected.

fields.status: The coloured dot: Online (green), Away (yellow), Do not disturb (red) or Invisible.
fields.activity: The word before your text: Playing, Streaming, Listening to, Watching or Competing in. "Just the text" shows only your text. "No activity" clears it.
fields.text: What it says after that word, like "my stream".
fields.streamUrl: Only for Streaming: your Twitch or YouTube channel link, so the status turns purple and links to it.
